(1) SS and UII peptides and their respective receptors are present in all vertebrate species; (2) these families are derived from a single ancestral pair that underwent two rounds of duplications; (3) the vertebrate ancestor had three SS peptides and six SSTRs, and four UIIs and five UTSRs; (4) in the teleost lineage all the genes were preserved except one SSTR4, whereas in mammals extensive losses occurred in both families.

the two G-protein-couple receptors families, SSTR and UTR2R, have been generated by a single ancestral ligands-receptor pair and then duplicated during vertebrate evolution, whereas the two peptide families, SS and UII, have been generated through local duplications and losses of the ancestral ligand.
